produced_by: genre-choice skill, run by a Claude Opus 5 agent with the repo as its working directory

image_prompt.text: A grid-based labyrinth of at least 36 identical interconnected rooms, each about 12x12 studs (4x4 metres), separated by walls with doorless rectangular openings between them
Openings cut so the identical rooms circle back into one another rather than dead-ending, keeping a wrong turn a short loop through the grid instead of a long backtrack
Uniform monolithic pale yellow (#d4c87a) drywall walls, damp and water-stained, slightly desaturated, with no windows and no doors anywhere
A low acoustic-tile drop ceiling about 10 feet (3 metres) high, carrying long rows of fluorescent tube light fixtures in cool white with a slight blue cast
Old beige commercial loop-pile carpet with a subtle repeating grey geometric pattern running unbroken across every room floor
Flat shadowless institutional lighting with desaturated, slightly sickly colour grading, so the whole labyrinth reads claustrophobic and unsettling

layout_placement.text: The ceiling tube fixtures actually emit cool white light, at a flicker amount that can be tuned

notes: Close classification call: the prompt is a place and a mood with no stated goal, threat, or win condition, so no-genre was a live option. Puzzle wins because the deliverable named is a labyrinth whose interconnected topology is the whole build, which is exactly what puzzle-maze describes. No pursuing threat is mentioned, so the genre note that sends chase pressure to Survival does not apply and no second genre was named.
Preset Maze / Labyrinth taken with its shape kept; its collectible-nodes option was dropped because the prompt asks for empty identical rooms with nothing to pick up.

Preset caveat from the loaded file: mazes invert the pipeline. The topology is generated procedurally first and dressed afterwards, because a free image cannot guarantee a traversable maze; the P6 here is not overridable.
Whole game is indoors with no exterior at all, so there is no outside-to-inside transition and no P3; building-interior was deliberately not used.

The Attributes to expose list (wallColor, carpetColor, ceilingHeight, lightFlickerIntensity, roomSize) is model parameterisation rather than layout geometry, so it is recorded here rather than as picks. The values themselves are carried in the image_prompt text: pale yellow #d4c87a walls, beige carpet, ~3 m ceiling, 12x12 stud rooms.

would have asked: Sounds like a Maze / Labyrinth build - a grid labyrinth whose topology is the puzzle, sealed interior throughout, with the openings placed so a wrong turn loops back instead of dead-ending. That has to be built structure-first so the rooms are guaranteed to interconnect. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: The prompt answers the shape, so only the Core puzzle options were open - solve gates, input slots, pressable inputs, clue walls. I took none of them, because a Backrooms Level 0 wander has nothing to solve. Would you want any of them, or does it stay a pure empty labyrinth?
would have asked: Is 'endless' literal? I built a finite grid of 36-plus rooms; if you want it to feel unbounded I would mirror or wrap the edges rather than change the shape.

would have asked: Anything else you want in the space? In particular, is there an entity or any chase pressure in here, and is there an exit? Either answer would add Survival as a second genre, so I did not assume one.
